changes.before: Keep each editable note attached to its record when reversing the list. Preserve initialCards order.
changes.after: Give each list item a stable key so its input stays with the right record.

before: A key identifies a sibling item across renders. Use a stable ID stored in the data, not the array position or a freshly generated random value. key is React’s identity hint; it is not passed as an ordinary prop, so Card receives the separate card prop.

cards.map(callback) calls the callback for each record and returns a new array of JSX elements. React renders those elements. Card destructures its card prop and returns one list item. The input deliberately uses defaultValue: it starts from that text, then the browser holds its edits. This makes identity visible when rows move. The defective starter uses cards.indexOf(card): indexOf returns this object’s current zero-based array position, which changes when the order changes. It is shown to explain the bug, not as a key recommendation. [...current] makes a shallow array copy; reverse() reverses that copy in place, leaving the original state array untouched.

Optional practice: Reverse twice and explain why the edited input returns to its first position. The checks cover these finite behaviors; a matching DOM alone does not prove every implementation choice. The frame supplies React and mounts App. No imports, server, persistence or network are involved.
after: A key tells React which item is which when a list changes. Use a stable ID from the record. Stable means it stays the same when the item moves. Its position in the list is not a stable ID.
`map` makes one component for each record. `key={card.id}` tells React the record's identity. The separate `card` prop gives `Card` its data; React does not pass key as an ordinary prop.
Two records can share a title and still need different keys. Their IDs keep them separate. `[...current]` copies the array before `reverse()` changes its order, so the original array stays unchanged.
Fix the key on each `Card`. The starter uses the item's current position, which changes after reversing. Use its record ID instead. Keep the original order of `initialCards`.

before.question: Two records share a title but have distinct stable IDs. Which key belongs on Card?
before.explanation: IDs distinguish records independently of title or position. Position keys can attach an existing input to the wrong record after reordering.

after.question: Two records have the same title but different stable IDs. Which key should each Card use?
after.explanation: The ID still identifies the same record after a move. A shared title cannot distinguish the two records.

project.title: Let each record own its key
project.task: Fix the keys so edited notes stay with their records after reversing. Keep the initialCards order unchanged.
project.done_when: An edited note travels with its record when the rows reverse, including when titles match.
